Glossary — what each figure counts

Every figure in the block above counts one physical object as one snag. Two identities hold, and both can be checked on the tiles above: the AI list splits into matched plus AI-only, and the consolidated defect list is every AI snag plus the manual snags nothing in the AI list answers. The matched counts differ between the two sides because a manual snag and an AI object are not the same grain — one snag is often answered by several objects, and one object by several snags. Two counts elsewhere on this page deliberately use a different unit and are labelled where they appear: scheduling lines (room × defect type) in the work-order roll-up, and table rows in the consolidated list, where one object may answer more than one manual snag.
Snag Recall 1 — the percentage of manually logged snags captured by AI with a useful description, defining the correct repair work, correct trade and location.
Snag Recall 2 — the percentage of manually logged snags captured by AI with complete semantic alignment: description, trade, snag classification, location and priority.
True positives — AI snags matched to a manual snag, plus the share of AI-only snags an automated reviewer confirmed as real defects on the evidence photograph.
False positives — AI snags an automated reviewer ruled not a defect on the photograph. Absence from the manual list is not evidence of a false positive: the manual walk is not a record of what is undamaged.
Snag Yield — true positives ÷ manual snag count × 100. Above 100% the AI list adds more real snags than the manual walk logged.

How these numbers are measured

Every figure on this page is produced by automated review and requires verification and validation by a DAMAC reviewer. The matching is done by an AI reviewer that sees only the two lists, not which method raised what, and rules each manual snag covered, partially covered or not covered on whether a contractor working the AI list would fix it — not on matching wording. Snag Recall 1 asks whether the AI entries define the correct repair work, trade and location; Snag Recall 2 additionally requires one of them to describe the identical defect. Snag Yield counts one physical object as one snag on both sides, over the recommended list, with audited false positives removed. Snags no photograph can settle — a tap test, an operation check, an element out of the camera's view — are set aside as not assessable and listed, never dropped. The recommended list is what was legible enough in the photographs to act on; a sampled review found that tier substantially more likely to be worth fixing than the rest, which are kept in their own section below.
